clue.text: Soft shoe shuffle? Comics can start off

indicators.note: the question mark turns the dance step into an instruction to mix the following letters
the start of the word can is taken off, leaving its last two letters

explanation.surface: A tap-dance routine is suggested to a comedian who wants to open a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft shoe shuffle' is a well-known dance, but 'shuffle' is the anagram signal. 'start off' drops the C from CAN, leaving AN; COMICS plus AN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft leather slipper of Native American origin, sewn without a hard sole.

clue.text: Concluded the actors were gloomy

parts.note: something concluded is finished, or over
the actors in a play make up its cast

explanation.surface: Once the play ended, the performers were downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied to the sky, the word means dull and cloudy, hence figuratively gloomy.

clue.text: Three schools to amalgamate? Put your shirt on it!

indicators.note: schools that amalgamate merge and are reorganised, so the letters before are mixed together

explanation.surface: A proposal to merge three schools is backed with total confidence, like a sure bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put your shirt on it' is British slang for betting everything, which makes the solver think of a racehorse; read literally, it is where you hang a shirt to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wooden frame for airing laundry, so it is literally a place to hang a shirt.

clue.text: He runs into resort guide

indicators.note: the words he and runs go into the resort word, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A man jogs into a holiday town where he works as a guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Himalayan mountaineering expeditions rely on these local people as guides and porters.

clue.text: Latin America protects a person's reputation

indicators.note: the words Latin America hold the answer inside them, as though protecting it

explanation.surface: A region of the world shields an individual's good standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's good standing is their good name, as in 'clear one's name'.

clue.text: Case of Commonwealth flyer becoming the head of the board

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, the first and last letters of Commonwealth

parts.note: an airman is a flyer, especially in an air force

explanation.surface: A Commonwealth pilot rises to lead a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who presides over a board of directors holds this title.

clue.text: Nothing very acceptable — my first egg

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word my

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their very first egg is perfectly acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a crossword convention for 'upper-class', so acceptable in polite society.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin biological term for a female reproductive cell, an unfertilised egg.

clue.text: Card player calling — and twisting!

parts.note: West is one of the four players at bridge, abbreviated W
ringing someone means calling them on the phone

explanation.surface: A bridge player shouts out a bid while squirming in their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so a card player can be any of N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wringing wet washing means wrenching and screwing it round to squeeze out water.

clue.text: A cold greeting, always, for the winner

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
hi is an informal greeting
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A champion is given a chilly reception every time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reaches their goals is a success, so a winner.

clue.text: Refuse to allow check on job centre

parts.note: to vet something is to check it carefully

indicators.note: the centre of the word job is its middle letter

explanation.surface: An employment office scrutinises applications before turning them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job centre' looks like the British employment office, but 'centre' simply picks the middle letter of 'job'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a veto is to forbid or block a proposal.

clue.text: Bearers of gifts who threw enemies into confusion

indicators.note: throwing something into confusion jumbles it, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gift-bringers caused chaos among their foes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the Nativity story are famous for bringing presents to the baby Jesus.

clue.text: Informative, hinting engel might be wrong

indicators.note: if the letters are wrong as they stand, they must be put in a different order

explanation.surface: A clue suggests that a person named Engel could be mistaken, which is illuminating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sheds light on a subject is instructive and informative.

clue.text: Game for a vulgar dance

parts.note: base means low or vulgar
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone is up for a crude bit of dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: This bat-and-ball sport is the national pastime of the United States.

clue.text: Permission to go away

definitions.meaning: ... as a noun is permission, as in 'by your ...'

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means authorised absence, permission; as a verb it means depart.

clue.text: Country constabulary taken in by endless letters

indicators.note: the constabulary word is taken inside the shortened letters word
endless means the last letter of the word for letters is removed

parts.note: mail is letters sent by post
the law is an informal name for the police

explanation.surface: Police are fooled by a stream of letters that never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked nation in south-east Africa, formerly Nyasaland.

clue.text: Eat out — and in France and Switzerland

parts.note: et is the French word for and
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A diner considers going out for a meal in France or Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' looks like dining at a restaurant, but it means corrode.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid used in engraving corrodes, or eats away, the surface of metal.

clue.text: It might make a life end!

definitions.text: It might make a life end!

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be made into another word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Something could bring someone's life to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the anagram of A LIFE END.
explanation.definitionFit: Raking gunfire along the length of a line of troops is deadly, so it can end a soldier's life.

clue.text: The strength of support won, oddly

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word won

explanation.surface: Victory came strangely through the power of one's backers.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular physical power is called brawn, as in 'brains and brawn'.

clue.text: City in bloom suppressing an aphid, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece pressing down on the others sits above them

parts.note: a bud is a bloom about to open
an aphid is an example of a garden pest

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a flower bud smothering a greenfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' reads as holding something down, but in a down clue it means one piece is written on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Hungary, on the Danube.

clue.text: Joke about new group

indicators.note: the joke word goes around the new letter, so it is placed about it

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone tells a joke about a fresh set of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a band of people acting together.

clue.text: The lack of touch, for example, is baloney!

parts.note: the prefix non- expresses the absence of something
touch is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Someone insists that numbness is all nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloney is slang for rubbish, foolish talk.

clue.text: Burnt trousers such as these

definitions.meaning: trousers whose legs widen towards the bottom

explanation.definitionFit: A fire flares when it blazes up, and bell-bottom trousers widen at the hem.

clue.text: Former stage profession that's very demanding

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
acting is the profession of the stage

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that their old theatre career was tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that requires great care and effort is strict and demanding.

clue.text: Tolerates assistants catching second-class

indicators.note: the assistants word catches the letter for second-class, holding it inside

parts.note: aides are assistants
B is a second-class grade

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with helpers who are second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to put up with it, as in 'I can't abide him'.

clue.text: City type's rival lined up for review

indicators.note: something put up for review is reworked, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A competitor from another city is lined up for inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City type' is a person from a particular city, here Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Liverpool is known by this name, informally a Scouser.

clue.text: A grip on immorality?

definitions.meaning: a tool with jaws that clamps and holds work steady

explanation.definitionFit: A bench clamp holds work steady, and wickedness is a moral failing; one word covers both.

clue.text: It sounds highly priced — a buck?

indicators.note: the clue says the word sounds like the next phrase, so a word of the same pronunciation is wanted

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: Something costly is being considered at a single dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: A buck looks like a dollar, but it is a male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male of the antlered animal family, so an example of the species.

clue.text: Eye proprietor is spoken of in island

indicators.note: the phrase is said out loud, giving the sound of a different word

parts.note: eye sounds the same as the letter I; a proprietor is an owner

explanation.surface: A person who owns an eye is mentioned as being on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation the R of 'owner' is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Hebridean island off Scotland's west coast, famous for St Columba's abbey.

clue.text: River bridges — category that's lost status

indicators.note: the river spans the category word, enclosing it as a bridge spans water

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a class is a category

explanation.surface: A rank sinks low among the bridges over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for someone who has fallen in social standing.

clue.text: Ruled, protecting society that's submissive

indicators.note: the word for ruled surrounds the society letter, protecting it

parts.note: a monarch who ruled reigned

explanation.surface: A monarch guarded a society that was meek.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has accepted something unwelcome without protest is passive and submissive.
